faqs.a: You must be paid at least £25,000 a year or the going rate for your occupation, whichever is higher. For most NHS clinical roles the operative figure is the national pay scale for your band and region. If the scale rate exceeds £25,000, the scale rate governs your application.
faqs.q: What salary do I need for the Health and Care Worker visa?

faqs.a: The long-standing requirement is English at CEFR B1 level across reading, writing, speaking and listening, proven by an approved test such as IELTS for UKVI or by a degree taught in English. Under the 2026 HC 1691 changes, first-time applicants are moving to B2, so confirm the current requirement on gov.uk.

New overseas applications for care workers and senior care workers closed on 22 July 2025. Those roles now allow in-country switches only until 22 July 2028 and cannot bring dependants. Nurses, doctors, midwives and allied health professionals with registration in hand can still apply from overseas.
faqs.q: Can care workers still apply in 2026?

faqs.a: The application fee is £304 for a visa of up to three years and £628 for longer stays. Holders are exempt from the Immigration Health Surcharge, saving about £1,035 per person per year. You must also show £1,270 in maintenance unless your sponsor certifies it.
faqs.q: How much does the visa cost?

faqs.a: After five years of continuous residence in the UK on this route, with continued sponsored employment, B1 English and the Life in the UK test, you can apply for indefinite leave to remain. The 2025 White Paper proposed a ten-year earned-settlement period, but the five-year rule still stands.

headline: UK Health and Care Worker Visa 2026: Salary & Requirements
metaDescription: UK Health and Care Worker visa 2026: £25,000 salary floor, B1 English, certificate of sponsorship, no health surcharge and 5 years to settlement. Guide.

sections.content:
The Health and Care Worker visa is the Skilled Worker route at a discount for clinical professions. It covers doctors, nurses, midwives, pharmacists, dentists and allied health professionals, with lower fees, a lower salary floor and exemption from the Immigration Health Surcharge.

You need a job offer in an eligible health or care occupation from an employer holding a Home Office sponsor licence, plus a certificate of sponsorship. The route is designed for the NHS, social care providers and other approved health and care sponsors.
sections.title: Who the visa is for

sections.content:
The general salary floor is £25,000 a year or the going rate for your occupation, whichever is higher. For most clinical roles the operative figure comes from the national pay scales, organised by NHS band and UK region, rather than the standard going-rates tables. Some roles outside the pay scales carry a £31,300 floor.

Eligible occupations are listed by SOC code, covering codes 2211 to 2259 for doctors and health professionals and 6131 to 6136 for care roles. Since 22 July 2025, new overseas applications closed for care workers and senior care workers, which now allow in-country switches only until 22 July 2028.
sections.title: Salary rules and eligible occupations

sections.content:
Applicants must prove English at CEFR B1 level, usually through an approved Secure English Language Test such as IELTS for UKVI or PTE Academic for UKVI, or with a degree taught in English. From 2026, first-time applicants are moving to B2 under the HC 1691 rule changes, so check the current level on gov.uk.

Most clinical roles also require professional registration, such as with the NMC for nurses or the GMC for doctors. You must also show £1,270 in maintenance held for 28 days, unless your sponsor certifies it on the certificate of sponsorship.
sections.title: English, registration and documents

sections.content:
Application fees are £304 for up to three years and £628 for more than three years, and holders are exempt from the Immigration Health Surcharge, saving about £1,035 a year per person. That makes this one of the cheapest UK work visas overall.

After five years of continuous residence with sponsored employment, B1 English and the Life in the UK test, you can apply for indefinite leave to remain. Time on this route counts as Skilled Worker time for settlement purposes.
